dedupe_keys.name: infrabel railway telecom network statistics gsm r base stations optical fibre length and transmission nodes belgium quarterly

description: Infrabel, the manager of the Belgian rail network, publishes two small quarterly series on its own telecommunication network on its open data portal. The GSM-R dataset counts the GSM-R base stations in service. GSM-R is the rail-only mobile radio system through which train drivers talk to the signal boxes that control traffic, and each antenna covers a stretch of line. The telecom infrastructure dataset gives the kilometres of optical fibre cable and the number of connected transmission nodes of the network that links Infrabel applications and staff. Each series has 44 quarterly rows (about eleven years). The GSM-R series was updated in August 2026 and the fibre series in July 2022. A related dataset traces the roll-out of ETCS train protection on the network. Coverage: Belgian rail network, national totals. Format and access: CSV, XLSX, JSON, Parquet and RDF exports and an Opendatasoft API, free under CC0 1.0. Caveats: national counts only, with no station locations or fibre routes; the fibre series may have stopped in 2022. Simulation uses: growth of a critical rail communication network for interdependency models between rail signalling and telecommunications, and a scale reference for GSM-R to FRMCS migration studies. Related records: the BIPT data portal includes mobile coverage measured along the Belgian rail network; the Dutch Antenneregister includes GSM-R sites in the Netherlands.
name: Infrabel railway telecom network statistics: GSM-R base stations, optical fibre length and transmission nodes (Belgium, quarterly)
